symmetryCheck: Control: the Congress-led UPA (2004–14), about which this file holds no theory. Applying the same lens — 'who got a resource without auction, and what did the auditor say' — produces a picture at least as alarming as the 2019–26 record: CAG's draft coal audit (2012) put undue benefit from 155 no-auction acreages at ₹10.67 lakh crore (final ₹1.86 lakh crore); JSPL (a sitting Congress MP's company) got a ~1,500 Mt coalfield in Feb 2009 that Coal India was refused; Hindalco's Talabira-II drew a CBI FIR naming K.M. Birla (closed 2014); Rungta Mines and Birla Corporation blocks were de-allocated; the Supreme Court cancelled 214 of 218 blocks in Sep 2014; and in Jul 2026 the SC accepted CBI's closure report on former PM Manmohan Singh for want of evidence. Vedanta's foundational benefit (HZL control for ₹445 crore) came under NDA-I in 2002 and its residual-stake decision under NDA-II in 2022 — the same beneficiary spans three governments. Conclusion: the 'promoter benefits under the party in power' lens is non-discriminating across regimes; what discriminates is whether the award was auctioned and whether an auditor or court later found the process defective. In the 2019–26 events here (Bihar PSA, JAL, PLI, DNH&DD) each was a multi-bidder process and no auditor finding exists yet; in the 2004–09 control the process was discretionary and the auditor and court did find it defective. The lens generates alarm in both; the record so far separates them.
